conclusion: DNSSEC validation failure at parent io.vn; Cloudflare authoritative A records, TLS and named tunnel are operational.
verified_findings: Cloudflare, Google and Quad9 validating resolvers return SERVFAIL with missing NSEC/invalid DS-denial proof.
Checking-disabled query returns existing Cloudflare A records.
Parent io.vn has authenticated DS records in vn, so its answers must validate.
Parent authorities return inconsistent DNSSEC material: a serves signatures; other tested servers omit signatures for SOA/DNSKEY; one SOA serial is behind.
Queries for ttech.io.vn DS omit the signed NSEC/NSEC3 denial proof, including direct TCP responses.
Both Cloudflare authoritative servers return the expected A records.
Pinning either Cloudflare A address while preserving hostname and verifying TLS yields HTTP 200 for /architecture/live.
Named connector has four ready connections, service has remained active since initial deployment and config mtime is unchanged.
Current server resolver is configured with DNSSEC=no/unsupported, explaining why local HTTP tests can succeed while validating resolvers fail.
inferences_and_limits: The exact onset and triggering upstream DNS change are not established; no registry change audit is available.
Resolver cache differences and validation settings can explain earlier/intermittent success; the phone resolver settings were not inspected.
Evidence localizes the problem to parent-zone DNSSEC service; it does not establish an operator incident announcement.
actions_taken: Read-only diagnostics; no DNS records, DNSSEC settings, tunnel config or services changed in this investigation.
recommended_action: Send parent-zone DNSSEC evidence to the domain registrar/provider for escalation to the io.vn/VNNIC DNS operator. Repair signing/denial proofs and synchronize authorities; then recheck validating public DNS. Keep the existing fallback tunnel for the presentation.
